I’m so glad I didn’t give up on the Galaxy Z Fold 8

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a phone that heavily tested my patience in the first few weeks, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 has become an all-time favorite.
  • The amount of hype this phone brought with it at launch was unreal.
  • I still believe the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is an excellent device.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a phone that heavily tested my patience in the first few weeks, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 has become an all-time favorite.

The amount of hype this phone brought with it at launch was unreal. Even then, I ultimately wound up going with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra of the two models Samsung released earlier this year. It’s a form factor I was used to, but only looking back now do I realize just how much I was missing out on.

I still believe the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is an excellent device. But the widely accepted blueprint for a consumer foldable might make a lateral move to what the Galaxy Z Fold 8 offers. That, I wouldn’t mind.

By comparison, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is tiny. Its front display is squared-up and offers less vertical real estate than any other mainstream device coming out of Samsung. But that’s even more true compared to the lengthy profile the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has. It’s called a “candy-bar foldable” for a reason.

The entire way I used my phone had to change, and the first few times I used the Galaxy Z Fold 8, I was left with a slightly bad taste in my mouth. I genuinely didn’t enjoy using it because of the amount of friction I was running into – not because the phone caused it, but because of my contradicting usage habits.

According to recent reports, I always felt like I was missing out on something with the smaller front display, and I stubbornly tried to use the inner display in its wide orientation for most applications. I considered switching back, but I’m glad I stuck with it.

On the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, or other standard foldables, I find myself using the inner display as the “main” display more often than not. But the Z Fold 8 gave me enough screen space in its closed state to come away with a good experience.

In a recent development, since release, the majority of apps I use have been optimized in Android 17, or One UI 9. Social apps work well because that little bit of extra width leaves breathing room for videos to expand and fill the screen. Shopping and productivity apps are similar, and everything seems to fall into place.

I hit a wall with the inner display, too. It took some time for me to realize using the Fold 8 in landscape was genuinely the wrong choice 70% of the time. It sounds weird, but a phone that was designed to open up to a wider inner screen offers a better experience when you rotate it. At that point, you’re getting the best part of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, without the other cons.

Obviously, the wide inner display is great for videos and multitasking – not as good as the Ultra. But the inner display in its relative portrait orientation is excellent on hand for apps that need a little more room. It essentially boils down to whether you want a big screen for what you’re using the outer display for – a crazy thought, but not always the user experience.

Sources indicate that now, the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s outer display feels like the upcoming normal to me, and using another phone feels foreign. The inner display has its place, and I automatically rotate it for nearly everything but media.

Even if this phone were just a proof of concept, it was successful. These smaller devices can work with some getting used to.

If given the choice between the design of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra once again, I’d now choose the smaller, wider Fold 8. Sure, it has a less capable camera loadout. The user experience does more to outweigh my ability to snap telephoto pictures, though.

This is a phone that has performed phenomenally in every major area, including how well it runs apps on Android and in battery life. I’m still getting more than a day’s worth of charge several months into using it. The same can’t be stated for the Galaxy Z Fold 7.

It’s possible Samsung is working on a next-gen Galaxy Z Fold 9 with the build of the Fold 8 and the camera power of an “Ultra” model, but there’s nothing concrete. Until then, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is riding the wave it created.

It has been revealed that on top of that, you get 16GB of onboard storage, which is double the amount on the cheaper model. This gives you more room to install apps and games without having to worry as much about running out of storage.

It has been revealed that you also get Wi-Fi 6E support, which can be particularly useful if you already have a compatible router at home. There's also Amazon's Fire TV Ambient Experience, which lets you turn your TV into a digital art display when you're not watching anything.

Of course, you still get all the features available on the cheaper model, including 4K streaming, Dolby Vision, HDR10+, Dolby Atmos, Alexa+ integration, and support for Xbox cloud gaming.

Shoppers ask AI for Black Friday deals, but few let the bots pay

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1004 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Traffic from AI services to US retail sites more than doubled on Thanksgiving from last year, Adobe told the Associated Press.
  • In a recent development, purchases made by AI agents are a far smaller slice.
  • Sources indicate that this weekend is the biggest test yet for the shopping agents from Meta, Google, OpenAI and Amazon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Traffic from AI services to US retail sites more than doubled on Thanksgiving from last year, Adobe told the Associated Press. Shoppers spent a record $7.1bn online that day, up 10.4%. Adobe expects $12.9bn on Black Friday itself.

In a recent development, purchases made by AI agents are a far smaller slice. They made up 0.4% of global e-commerce transactions and 0.2% of their value, according to Bain & Co research. Annie Palmer reported the figures for CNBC.

Sources indicate that this weekend is the biggest test yet for the shopping agents from Meta, Google, OpenAI and Amazon. Each wants to help people find gifts and, in time, buy them. The early evidence points to three problems. Shoppers do not trust the bots with their money. Many retailers will not let them in. And nobody agrees who pays when an agent gets it wrong.

Sources indicate that A Morning Consult poll for Visa found that 54% of adults have used AI for at least one shopping task, up from 47% last year. Only 23% trust generative AI to make payments for them, Phil Wahba reported for Fortune.

According to recent reports, the price of the item matters too. In an American Express survey, 52% of US consumers were happy for an agent to buy cheap items such as groceries. Only 15% felt the same about electronics and appliances, the massive sellers of Black Friday.

Sources indicate that that caution has some basis. Visa sent 22 AI models on 15 shopping tasks earlier this month, and they failed 42.8% of their runs. In more than half of the failed runs, the agent still bought something.

British shoppers are trying the tools too. Meta released Muse in the UK this week, with partners including Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury’s, JD Sports and Currys. A third of people planning to shop in the sales intend to use AI, up from 19% last year, according to a YouGov poll. Almost half of the shoppers who use AI worry about biased or sponsored results, Sarah Butler reported in The Guardian.

Even shoppers who want an agent to buy for them may find it cannot. About half of major retailers and popular brands do not let AI assistants shop their sites. London software firm Human Forward found this after testing ChatGPT, Gemini, Muse and other agents on 200 websites, Spencer Soper reported for Bloomberg.

Recent findings suggest that amazon has gone furthest. It blocked Muse from its store in September. It is also suing Perplexity over the shopping agent in its Comet browser, in a case due for trial next year. Amazon is reportedly in talks with Meta about Muse, but the block is still in place.

“Agentic third-party applications such as Muse have the same obligations, and we’ve requested that Meta remove Amazon from the experience,” an Amazon spokesperson told Bloomberg.

In a recent development, amazon’s advertising business is expected to bring in $81.9bn this year, Bloomberg reported. Bots that browse for shoppers could undercut it. Chief executive Andy Jassy told investors in October that outside agents were not meaningfully hurting its ads business.

“The natural question is whether agentic shopping from external horizontal agents is meaningfully impacting Amazon ads, and the answer is no,” Jassy noted on Amazon’s earnings call.

Other companies limit agents rather than ban them. eBay, United Airlines and Kohl’s restrict what agents can do or block them, CNBC reported. Some retailers let bots browse but stop them at the checkout. Agents that do get in can still get stuck at logins and CAPTCHA tests.

Maia Bittner, chief product officer at fintech startup Imprint, told CNBC she asked Muse to buy windscreen wipers from AutoZone. Seventeen hours later, the agent stated AutoZone had cancelled the order over an error. Its suggestion was to buy them on Amazon herself.

Sources indicate that the bigger question for retailers is liability. Some have written their answer into their terms of service. Best Buy treats an agent’s purchases as if the customer had made them.

“Best Buy is not responsible for conduct, errors, actions, or inaction by any Digital Agent,” the company’s terms state.

Card and payment companies are taking on some of that risk. American Express has remarked it will protect eligible customers from charges caused by an agent’s errors. Stripe, whose Link wallet works with Muse, offers a refund guarantee on some agent purchases. JPMorgan Chase went the other way last month and blocked outside agents from acting for its customers, citing security, CNBC reported.

In a recent development, in the UK, TrueLayer is testing another route. Its pilot lets an agent pay by bank at Papa John’s, under the FCA’s watch.

“In Europe especially, retailers are asking a simple question: if the bot gets it wrong, who’s liable?” Mark Howell, director of European retail at e-commerce firm Rithum, told The Guardian.

Recent findings suggest that meta says that in the UK, Muse must ask for approval before it buys anything. A separate “security agent” checks its actions against the permissions a user has granted.

The tech companies are pressing on. Muse reached 10 million owners in the US and Canada about six weeks after its September launch, Bloomberg reported. Mark Zuckerberg told investors in October that shopping was its most common use, with users spending $200 on average. He expects Meta to take a small fee from transactions. Google has rolled out Universal Cart, which puts items from several retailers in one basket.

McKinsey estimates agentic commerce could generate $1tn of US economic activity by 2030. Retailers, meanwhile, are bracing for more AI-driven cyberattacks around the sales.

It has been revealed that matt Kochmann, a tech executive, tried ChatGPT, Muse and Claude to find a case for his upcoming iPhone. None of them stood out, he told Bloomberg.

“It just doesn’t feel magical yet,” he said.

CNET Survey: $75 Billion in Packages Could Be at Risk of Holiday Porch Theft

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1583 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Major holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a proposal to protect your package from porch pirates.
  • CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts.
  • But leaving your packages up for grabs could be a massive risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Major holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a proposal to protect your package from porch pirates.

CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts. This year, the average package value is $276.24, and 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or caught an attempted theft within the past year. Yet 20% of US adults don’t use security devices due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees.

But leaving your packages up for grabs could be a massive risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered. On the other hand, some bad actors don’t seem to mind being caught in the act on home security cameras, so are they really enough to deter bad actors? And what more can you do to protect your deliveries?

CNET’s findings show that some US adults have dealt with porch theft firsthand: 8% had packages meant for themselves or their households stolen within the past year, and 5% had a delivered gift stolen. Very few (1%) caught a theft in the act on a video doorbell or security camera.

Meanwhile, many US adults know someone who fell victim to package theft — 13% know a neighbor or community member who had a package stolen within the past year, and 12% know someone who doesn’t live in their community who has.

“Close to a third of our respondents are personally acquainted with package theft, which is still a high number compared to other issues like break-ins,” said CNET’s senior home security editor, Tyler Lacoma. “Thieves generally look for crimes of opportunity, and few things are easier than a package left on a doorstep, especially if nobody is home.”.

Surprisingly, most US adults (72%) haven’t experienced package theft or know anyone who has.

Even though the percentages above may seem low, Lacoma mentioned that package theft typically increases during the holidays when thieves know more deliveries are likely, and newly introduced porch theft tactics are always on the horizon.

Sources indicate that there are reports of thieves trying Wi-Fi jamming to disable live security camera footage while they steal packages. And findings show that some are installing spy cams in high-value neighborhoods to learn your home’s layout and habits to take your packages shortly after they’re delivered. In recent years, pirates have even tracked shipping labels for high-value tech, like iPhones, to steal the package within minutes of arrival.

In a recent development, so while the majority of US adults haven’t fallen victim, that shouldn’t be a sign to shrug off the concern or relax your home security measures. Instead, now’s the time to plan how to safely store your packages if they’re delivered while you’re away.

Online shopping and deliveries to your door can be a convenient way to check off holiday wish lists, but the average package value this holiday season is less than last year. CNET found that US adults blueprint to have an average of $276.24 in holiday packages delivered during this holiday season. That’s $23.82 less than last year’s average of $300.06.

Industry observers note that by generation, Millennials also have a lower estimated average package value than last year, with an average of $227.25, compared to their 2025 package value of $307.47 — an $80.22 difference, while Gen Z’s package value is only about $7 less than last year. But any package’s value is still worth taking precautions to help prevent it from being stolen.

According to recent reports, lacoma has thoughts on why that might be. In short, lower spending could mean fewer packages.

Sources indicate that “I wonder if people have also simply gotten fewer packages in general this year due to tariffs, inflation and tech prices. That could pull these numbers down,” said Lacoma. But there’s a high chance that could be the case considering CNET’s 2026 annual holiday survey, which found that US adult tech spending is down to $808 — which is $123 less than last year’s average of $931.

Thieves may not always know what’s in boxes they’re stealing but they’re willing to take a chance. We asked US adults which items were stolen in package thefts in the past year to give you a sense of what’s at risk.

Among the items stolen, apparel and accessories were the most common goods stolen (40%). That’s followed by toys and games (23%). Then there are everyday home basics, like decor, cookware and small appliances (19%).

It has been revealed that but personal tech devices and accessories are still among the items stolen. Small accessories like phone chargers and cases are most common (16%) among tech-related packages stolen. They are followed by audio gadgets like headphones and Bluetooth speakers, along with streaming devices and soundbars (11%, respectively).

Still, more costly tech like gaming consoles (10%), computers and laptops (9%) and smart home devices (6%) are among devices stolen.

You shouldn’t leave your packages up to chance. That’s why Lacoma recommends a few safer options to ensure your packages are stored securely after they’re delivered, even beyond keeping an eye on your doorbell or security camera. Instead, keep your packages out of sight with tactics like a delivery box with a code or key or ask for an in-garage delivery.

Recent findings suggest that “Delivery boxes have reached a newly introduced level of popularity in recent years as an effective way to stop porch pirates completely. However, Amazon’s Key service that delivers to your garage is an alternative,” said Lacoma. “Either way, you’ll need to trust delivery people to handle your shipments, unless you want to arrange for pickup at a nearby shipping center, which some people like to combine with other holiday errands.”.

If you don’t want to install a new security feature, try scheduling your packages to arrive when you know you’re home, requiring a signature from someone you trust or changing your delivery location to a pickup spot, like UPS’ Hold for Pick-Up locations or Amazon Lockers.

Sources indicate that home surveillance, like outdoor security cameras and video doorbells, can deter package thieves who don’t want to risk getting caught on camera. But US adults have mixed feelings about their effectiveness in protecting against package theft.

There are two deterrents that are keeping US adults from having security devices — cost and privacy. Findings show that 20% of US adults lack home security measures due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees. That’s followed by 9% who don’t want to use cameras because of privacy concerns.

“Fortunately, the right home security picks can solve both these problems,” noted Lacoma. “Brands like Tapo, Eufy, Aqara and even Google Nest offer package detection and alerts for free, so you don’t have to worry about extra fees.”.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for a camera that’s off-the-grid, consider the Arlo Go 2. It’s an LTE camera, so it uses a cellular data connection instead of Wi-Fi. It still finds a signal, supports app operation and live video viewing. If you’re looking for a power-over-Ethernet camera that uses a cable connection, the Reolink Duo 3 is a good choice.

Lacoma added that many companies also offer ways to use local video storage and local AI detection so nothing is stored in the cloud. There are also features, such as customizable privacy zones, to minimize privacy concerns when used with the right precautions.

Industry observers note that among all US adults, only 14% have security devices with a monthly subscription that lets them save or playback video. By comparison, 12% have security devices but no subscription.

It has been revealed that those percentages could be low for a few reasons, including the overall perception of how helpful surveillance and security really are against porch theft. Eleven percent of US adults don’t think security devices deter porch thefts. It’s a valid concern since 4% fell victim to package theft or an attempted theft despite having security devices. And some US adults (9%) use security devices to get proof of a theft after the fact — not to prevent it.

But that doesn’t mean you should ignore the possibility of package theft — especially during the holidays. Even if you don’t want to install cameras or new security devices, make a proposal to protect your packages and avoid the headache of package theft over the holidays.

It has been revealed that “Remember, the simple presence of a security camera is enough to make many thieves look elsewhere – interviews have confirmed it,” mentioned Lacoma. “And with today’s phone alerts about package detection, you can usually check on a package only seconds after it appears, or bring up footage if it unexpectedly vanishes, letting you take action fast. Upcoming practices like delivery boxes or in-garage delivery help address risks in concrete ways, too.”.

Recent findings suggest that CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,016 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken between Oct. 23–27, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus).

The $75 billion figure was calculated by multiplying the average value of deliveries each US adult expects to receive by the 2025 US population of adults ages 18 and over calculated by the US Census Bureau.

As OxygenOS is slowly being replaced by ColorOS on OnePlus devices, long-time OnePlus fans are expressing their disappointment with several missing OnePlus features.

According to recent reports, if you’re a OnePlus user who has enjoyed 3D Wallpaper and AI Motion Wallpaper, per-game performance modes, Mind Pilot, AI Photo Agent, the OnePlus Dialer, lock screen music lyrics, or even the OnePlus calculator Easter egg, you may soon be joining the ranks of OnePlus fans who are finding the ColorOS 17 enhancement more than a little disappointing. Several fan-favorite features like the ones previously mentioned are either not available at all in ColorOS 17, or are only available in some regions.

Industry observers note that onePlus ran a ColorOS 17 AMA on November 23, but failed to clearly answer many of the questions put forth by the community. Essentially, the answer for most of these missing features runs along the lines of “we’re working on it, but availability will depend on your region.” The ColorOS 17 global rollout has been slower than initially anticipated, and my own OnePlus 13 has yet to receive the update at all.

Other models, like the OnePlus 15, are now receiving the updated builds of ColorOS 17 in Europe and some other regions, which include a few feature additions and bug fixes, but don’t look to resolve the biggest complaints raised during the AMA. OnePlus officially shut down its presence in North America, Europe, India, and other regions back in July, and Oppo has taken over software updates since then, swapping out OnePlus’s OxygenOS Android build with Oppo’s ColorOS.

Review: Aqara W200 supports Adaptive Temperature in HomeKit at a great price

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that earlier this year, my wife and I bought our first house.
  • Industry observers note that one of the most important and useful smart home accessories is a smart thermostat.
  • According to recent reports, installing the Aqara W200 was relatively straightforward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that earlier this year, my wife and I bought our first house. Along with all the other exciting things, it’s also let me spend a lot of time testing newly introduced smart home gear.

Industry observers note that one of the most important and useful smart home accessories is a smart thermostat. Six months ago, I installed the Aqara Smart Thermostat W200, and it’s been a fantastic addition to our smart home setup … especially because it supports Apple’s Adaptive Temperature feature. Here’s how it works.

According to recent reports, installing the Aqara W200 was relatively straightforward. I’d previously installed various Ecobee thermostats. The trickiest part this time was learning the intricacies of the new house itself, which the Aqara app did a good job of guiding me through.

It has been revealed that I used the Aqara app for the installation and setup, like choosing an interface design for the thermostat’s display itself. But after that, I closed the app and haven’t opened it since. Everything now is managed through the Apple Home app, and I appreciate that the Aqara app lets me do this without any pushback. It doesn’t try to pull me back into it to sell me a subscription or show me ads.

This matters because the Aqara app is nothing to write home about. It has a lot of settings, but I don’t think it’s particularly elegant or user-friendly. You can choose from a small collection of different screensavers. The thermostat’s interface is similar to the app in that it’s very utilitarian, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing for quick manual temperature adjustments.

The Aqara W200 also has a mmWave radar sensor that detects your presence. When you walk up to it, that sensor detects your approach and the screensaver automatically goes away to reveal the controls. It’s also exposed to HomeKit and can trigger automations. Unfortunately, this isn’t particularly useful for me because of the thermostat’s awkward location.

According to recent reports, the Aqara W200’s build quality is good enough. It’s primarily made of plastic, unlike higher-end smart thermostats that feature metal housing, so it doesn’t look super premium on your wall. It has a responsive 4-inch touchscreen. It has a small footprint overall, so you’ll likely need the included back trim plate if your previous thermostat required a larger opening in the wall.

In a recent development, the standout feature of the Aqara W200, though, is its support for Apple’s Adaptive Temperature feature, which debuted as part of iOS 26. As of right now, the Aqara W200 is the only thermostat with Adaptive Temperature support available, though two more are coming next year as part of Apple’s new Home Collection suite.

Adaptive Temperature is Apple’s feature that will automatically adjust your thermostat’s temperature based on your preferences. It uses your location and the location of other home members to determine when to adjust the thermostat.

Once you enable Adaptive Temperature, you set your ideal temperature range for the following states:.

My wife and I set our preferred temperature ranges for each scenario. I particularly appreciate the ability to set a different range for night, since we like it noticeably colder overnight than during the day.

After that setup process, Adaptive Temperature has worked in the background without any involvement from us. It passively uses all the information on our iPhones to make its decision.

“Your iPhone uses on-device intelligence to predict when you’re on your way home to bring it to the correct temperature by the time you get there, and adjusts the thermostat to save energy when you are far away from home,” Apple explains.

Recent findings suggest that adaptive Temperature uses your iPhone and other home members’ devices to determine when to adjust the temperature. “Home can learn daily routines to predict when you’re likely to arrive and adjust the temperature for you,” Apple says. This includes things like your calendar events.

I can count on one hand the number of times we’ve had to manually adjust the thermostat since installing the W200, and most of those times were because we had guests with different preferences than ours.

Honestly, I thought I wrote this post months ago, but I guess it slipped my mind. I actually think there’s a pretty simple explanation for that, though. I installed the W200, enabled Adaptive Temperature in the Apple Home app, and haven’t thought about it since.

I think that’s a great endorsement of the Aqara W200 as a product. When I build a smart home, I want accessories that I can install, benefit from the “smarts” of, and never have to think about. That’s why I’ve also come to appreciate Lutron, which I’ve installed throughout my entire house. The Aqara W200 falls into that same bucket.

Between the Smart Thermostat W200 and UWB Smart Lock U400 (full review), Aqara powers two key pillars of my smart home, and I’ve been incredibly impressed with both.

Recent findings suggest that the Aqara Smart Thermostat W200 is also very reasonably priced. It retails for $159.99, but is presently on sale for $119.99.

Here are a few other smart home products that I’ve installed since we bought our house:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xpeng’s robots over the years, with the latest Iron humanoid on the far right.

Industry observers note that chinese EV maker Xpeng will start mass-producing its Iron humanoid robot in January 2027 and train it as a store assistant first. Its co-president Brian Gu states it could reach homes in one or two years, priced like one of Xpeng’s cars, with tens of thousands of sales targeted next year.

Chinese EV maker Xpeng will start mass-producing its Iron humanoid robot in January, the organization noted at its AI Day this week. Co-president Brian Gu told CNBC it could be doing household chores in “one or two years”.

Sources indicate that first, Iron will train as a store assistant in Xpeng’s shops from early 2027. Gu said the tech giant could then “start thinking about deploying into home settings”.

It has been revealed that the robot has 76 degrees of freedom, the separate ways its body can move, and more than 1,500 touch sensors. It runs on three of Xpeng’s own Turing AI chips, the same family it puts in its cars. Xpeng’s new production line is designed to finish one every 2.5 minutes at full speed.

In a recent development, gu told Bloomberg TV that Xpeng aims to sell “tens of thousands” of Iron robots in 2027, with public sales from the second quarter. He expects it to cost about as much as one of Xpeng’s cars, which sell for 119,800 yuan (about $18,000) to 309,800 yuan.

“It’s much easier to be profitable for the robotics business than the autos business,” Gu told CNBC.

Recent findings suggest that xpeng’s robotics unit raised more than $900M in August ahead of the production run. Rival carmaker BYD has also been readying a humanoid for its showrooms.

Xpeng is one of many Chinese firms racing to scale up. Morgan Stanley expects China to ship 50,000 humanoids this year, and Chinese firms already build almost every humanoid sold worldwide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Tuesday, Bambu Lab took the wraps off its third-generation 3D printer, the P3C. It brings to the mainstream the tech giant’s “tool changer” technology, which was previously reserved for higher-end, flagship models like the $2,500 H3C. Given the P3C costs less than half the bigger model, it might be the perfect gift to get your favorite 3D printing hobbyist for Black Friday.

According to recent reports, the substantial deal here is the introduction of the Swaptek 7-tool changer, which allows you to switch to a different color or material in just 6 seconds, preventing you from having to stop and clean the nozzle every time. The technology produces significantly less waste and allows you to create faster prints.

Recent findings suggest that the tool changer technology also allows you to mix different materials with less of a fuss, so you can use a typical rigid plastic and something like a flexible rubber in a single pass without stopping. It can switch between different nozzle sizes in one job. You can switch between  0.2 mm, 0.4 mm, 0.6 mm and 0.8 mm midprint.

Recent findings suggest that the P3C ships with an integrated sealed AMS 3P filament management system that can store up to seven spools, each of which is on an independent feed path to the printer. You can also connect up to four external AMS units, supporting up to 22 colors.

The P3C is more than just a 3D printer. The Swaptek system supports interchangeable craft tools, letting you cut, draw or emboss on materials.

Bambu Lab also included a few features that make the P3C more approachable to newcomers. The P3C provides full-auto calibration, automatically aligning nozzle offsets and multi-tool heads so you don’t have to do it yourself. There’s also a built-in AI monitoring system that can detect issues like nozzle clogs and purge-bin jams early on. A new health management system will no longer spit out vague or obscure errors when something goes wrong. Instead, the new system will explain the matter in plain language and provide step-by-step troubleshooting right on the screen.

In a recent development, CNET’s 3D printing expert, James Bricknell, hasn’t been able to test Bambu Labs’ latest model yet but is excited about it. “While the P3C didn’t arrive in time for a hands-on, it’s built with the same design language and hardware support as the recently released H3C. If it is anywhere near as good, and I think that’s likely, it’ll be at the top of any serious 3D printing enthusiast’s wish list.”.

According to recent reports, the P3C 3D printer AMS combo is available now worldwide for $1,149. The combo includes the printer, AMS 3P as well as 5 0.4mm standard PrintTools. Two slots are left open for you to customize. This combo option comes with virtually everything you need to get started printing your works of art and more.

We’re on the hunt for researchers and founders who are engineering solutions to society’s most formidable problems, from human disease to climate change. We also recognize those who have made clever and useful inventions, key fresh scientific discoveries, or technological breakthroughs early in their careers.

Nominees can be based anywhere in the world, but must be under 35 on October 1, 2027. Have someone in mind? Or think you’d be a great candidate and want to put yourself forward? Here's how to make a nomination for our 2027 list.

According to recent reports, there are a lot of remarkable things about Avi Davidson. A horrific injury as a teenager left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Today, his experience informs his work as a trauma therapist. He's also taking part in a clinical trial of newly introduced tech that allows him to move—and feel with—a prosthetic hand.Before the trial started, researchers scanned his brain to see how his missing left hand was represented in his brain. Will that change? And what might that mean for people who are born without limbs?

Here’s what a bionic hand might reveal about the mind.

  • OpenAI has launched a latest legal action against Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers, in an effort to “compete unfairly by any means available”.
  • The ChatGPT maker filed the lawsuit in a California court on Friday, striking back after the iPhone maker accused the AI lab of stealing top-secret information this summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that openAI has countersued Apple, accusing the iPhone maker of stealing trade secrets and threatening suppliers working on its upcoming devices. The filing escalates a legal fight that began with Apple’s lawsuit against OpenAI in July.

OpenAI has launched a latest legal action against Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers, in an effort to “compete unfairly by any means available”.

The ChatGPT maker filed the lawsuit in a California court on Friday, striking back after the iPhone maker accused the AI lab of stealing top-secret information this summer.

According to the report, OpenAI alleges Apple is “coercing and threatening” suppliers working with the ChatGPT maker. Its hardware ambitions include new personal devices following last year’s acquisition of Jony Ive’s “io” firm.

It has been revealed that the complaint also claims Apple encouraged employees to store corporate files on personal devices and cloud accounts. OpenAI has previously characterized Apple’s case as an attempt to stop it from hiring Apple employees.

It has been revealed that apple’s original lawsuit names OpenAI, io Products, and former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan. Tan previously led iPhone and Apple Watch product design at Apple.

According to recent reports, apple alleges confidential engineering information and hardware development details were taken to benefit OpenAI’s consumer device efforts. OpenAI has disputed those allegations.

It has been revealed that the new action also follows OpenAI’s October claim that an employee who returned to Apple sent more than 100 confidential files about unreleased OpenAI hardware to personal accounts. Those files allegedly included device images, engineering data, and supplier information.

Recent findings suggest that apple responded at the time that its investigation had not located OpenAI confidential information. The company noted it requested more specific information to continue searching and would work with OpenAI to investigate the allegations.

Meanwhile, Apple has sought a preliminary injunction to prevent further use of its alleged trade secrets and won expanded access to evidence during discovery.

Apple’s original case is scheduled to go to trial on July 19, 2027.

It features 24 single-sided cups, which allow you to stick your phone to a mirror, window, or any other surface you think will provide that perfect TikTok angle.

Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you initiative to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and Dreamworks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.

The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.

Industry observers note that the Fanttik X9 Pro can inflate a car tire in under a minute, making routine maintenance fast and easy. There are four one-click presets for cars, motorcycles, bikes, and balls, along with a manual mode that reaches a maximum pressure of 150 PSI.

It has been revealed that apple’s 11th-gen iPad is the successor to the previous 10-gen model. It has a new A16 chip and few other changes — and is the only Apple tablet to not support Apple Intelligence.

No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

According to recent reports, sony’s XM4 noise-canceling headphones were so good, the organization brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.

Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

Compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (presently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches).

Sources indicate that the water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.

Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

The Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for new users. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.

007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

Industry observers note that amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.

Sources indicate that the cost continues to fall on Samsung’s latest, best foldable yet. The Z Fold 8 is a passport-style phone, like the iPhone Duo, with fast performance and slick design.

Recent findings suggest that you likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

Sources indicate that acer’s answer to the MacBook Neo, with an Intel Core 5 processor, 8GB of RAM, 120Hz display, and speedy Thunderbolt 4 ports. We’re still testing this one, but it’s showing promise for an affordable choice.

It has been revealed that outside of the Integrity, few spacecraft made as big a splash in 2026 as the one Ryland Grace piloted in Project Hail Mary. And now, thanks to Lego, you can construct a microscale replica of the titular Hail Mary, complete with a miniature Rocky figure.

Hoto’s rechargeable screwdriver is ideal for small repairs. It offers three torque modes, a rotational speed of up to 220RPM, and a helpful circular LED to illuminate dark spaces. The durable case also holds all 25 steel bits and an extension bar for getting into hard-to-reach places.

According to recent reports, sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

According to recent reports, apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.

One of the most affordable Tandem RGB Stripe OLEDs is even cheaper during Black Friday. The AW3226Q monitor has a 165Hz refresh rate, G-Sync compatibility, better-looking text rendering than most other OLED monitors, and unbeatable contrast.

JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.

The latest super-rugged wearable from Apple features better battery life than the previous version, plus AI-powered features like Siri Recap also available on the Series 12.

Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.

Industry observers note that hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.

According to recent reports, the Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.

According to recent reports, moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.

Industry observers note that bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”.

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

Garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.

Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.

TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

Sources indicate that google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.

Roku now makes some of the most affordable, yet feature-packed 4K OLED TVs available for gamers or movie lovers looking for a big TV upgrade under $1,000. The Pro Series LX with better brightness, faster refresh rate, and a polarizer to reduce reflections starts at $200 more.

Sources indicate that if you’re on a tight budget, but want spectacular contrast and brightness control that only an OLED can provide, here’s a deal for you. Alienware’s 1440p 27-inch QD-OLED monitor with 240Hz refresh rate is selling at its lowest price yet. Read our hands-on.

Sources indicate that the best XPS 13 in years. It doesn’t have a headphone jack and starts with only 8GB of RAM but it’s an excellent thin-and-light with a great screen, a solid Intel chip, and speedy storage.

Sources indicate that soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for less than Apple’s latest AirPods.

In a recent development, the latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review.

Industry observers note that the significant difference between the Superstrike and other gaming mice lies beneath its main two mouse buttons. It uses haptic actuators instead of mechanical switches, allowing for lower latency and more longevity.

A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.

Sources indicate that the Nex Playground’s motion-controlled gameplay is designed for ages five and up. It comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe, but many more titles are available via a subscription. It’s a ton of fun for kids. This is the lowest price so far in 2026. Read our review.

In a recent development, nothing has changed in terms of aesthetics, but the Max 2 deliver better sound and some upcoming features. Not exactly worth upgrading for, but fantastic for those who are considering them now. Read our full review.

It’s hard to find a cooler lamp than Govee’s Uplighter floor lamp at this price. It can light a room, and display a mesmerizing pattern up your wall and onto your ceiling.

Recent findings suggest that the Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.

Sources indicate that sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.

The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.

Sources indicate that donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Paulene’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.

Industry observers note that arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has recreated here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.

Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.

A 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen that comes in a few design options. It’s a frame that features Alexa, and doubles as a smart speaker. It works with Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members.

This innovative new smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It also works with the new Aliro standard, making it compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking. Read our review.

Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.

In Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time.

Birdbuddy’s charming, camera-equipped feeder identifies and snaps shots of each bird that stops by, supplementing its 5-megapixel stills with insightful facts via an app. The solar roof helps keep the camera’s battery topped up even when it’s cloudy outside.

According to recent reports, azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.

Magna-Tiles are a quintessential kids’ toy. The colorful, semi-translucent geometric shapes are a favorite here at The Verge, especially for those of us who prefer the simplicity of building with magnets rather than bricks.

Lego’s 709-piece kit lets you construct three brick-ified bonsai trees, including a black pine, a ginkgo with yellow leaves, and a wisteria with hanging lilac flowers. It also comes with three ornamental displays, just in case you want a raised stand on which to showcase them.

Recent findings suggest that the Beam isn’t as powerful as the Sonos Arc, nor can it match the flagship soundbar’s Dolby Atmos immersion bubble. But you still get room-filling surround sound for less money — and the Beam ties into the Sonos ecosystem for added convenience. Read our review.

It has been revealed that google wants to sell you on the Pro’s software features, but it’s the underlying hardware that makes it a stellar Android handset. The build quality is incredible, the larger telephoto sensor is an improvement, and it now supports faster wired speeds and Qi2.2 for up to 25W wireless charging. Read our review.

Industry observers note that roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design. Read our review.

The Insta360 Link 2 offers the same auto-swiveling design as its excellent predecessor, only in a smaller form factor. It also offers a slate of newly introduced features, including group tracking and no-follow zones.

With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

Industry observers note that these smart lights have beautiful colors, a nice selection of festive scenes, and an easy-to-use app. They are super reliable when paired with a Hue Bridge and also work over Bluetooth. They come in three lengths, work with all the major smart home platforms, and are Matter-compatible. Read our review.

Recent findings suggest that the Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s newly introduced AZ3 chip. Read our review.

Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.

According to recent reports, vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan, but it is far more interesting.

A quiet, battery-powered fan that moves a lot of air despite its small size, the Switchbot Standing Circulator is a surprisingly versatile smart home addition.

According to recent reports, the last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.

Sources indicate that fairphone’s latest is a very light revision to the 6, adding a newer processor and carrying forward its repairability and ethical values. Tradeoffs compared to a traditional smartphone are few, and the benefits are real.

According to recent reports, the proliferation of miniature screens continues with Ugreen’s latest Nexode USB-C Cable, which features a full-color LCD screen on one end that displays current power draw (up to 240W). It also supports 480Mbps data transfer speeds and, unlike similar power meter-equipped cables, lets you turn off the screen when needed.

In a recent development, the Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.

It has been revealed that nintendo’s latest Pokémon spinoff for the Switch 2 is part Pokémon, part Minecraft, and part Animal Crossing. Yet, despite borrowing gameplay mechanics from each, the cozy life sim is more than the sum of its expansive, building-centric parts. It’s breezy and warm-hearted, with enough secrets to keep mother dearest occupied for hours on end.

Recent findings suggest that google’s fresh Pixel 10A introduces faster wired charging, Satellite SOS, and new AI tools like Camera Coach and Auto Best Take. Otherwise, it’s basically the Pixel 9A, with the same Tensor G4 chip and a dual-camera system. Read our review.

The entry-point into RTX Spark laptops, the Asus ProArt is a creator-focused MacBook Pro wannabe with a sleek blacked-out design and lovely OLED display. Read our initial Nvidia RTX Spark hands-on.

According to recent reports, there are many gaming headsets out there, but few as elegant as Fractal’s Scape. The PC-focused (but Switch- and PlayStation-compatible) wireless headset offer great sound and include a wireless charger, and they have easy-to-master physical controls.

Everyone knows gift cards aren’t the best gift, but with such steep discounts happening on Nintendo eShop credit, you can save a lot on a Switch 2, or games and accessories, if you’re alright with jumping through a couple extra hoops.

According to recent reports, USB-C display glasses can make travel (or relaxing on the couch) more fun by putting a huge virtual screen in front of your face. Xreal’s One Pro are some of the best out there at displaying content from your phone, tablet, laptop, or portable handheld.

Sources indicate that govee’s Permanent Outdoor Lights 2 are Matter-ready smart lights you can leave up year-round. They can display multiple colors at once, with 100 preset lighting scenes, customizable effects, and the ability to sync to music. The lights also feature an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance.

Sources indicate that the Ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium is an excellent option for adding smarts and some style to your HVAC system. As well as being a smart way to control your energy use, the thermostat can also act as a video intercom for Ecobee’s excellent doorbell camera and an indoor air quality monitor. Read our review.

Revision, November 27th: Updated to include several fresh picks, including those for Govee’s Permanent Outdoor Lights 2 and the Ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium.

Black Friday headphones deals started out strong earlier this month, but now that it's actually Black Friday, they're even better.

According to recent reports, take, for instance, the 45% discount on the second-generation Bose QuietComfort headphones (released just this past August, btw). Prefer a flagship model? No problem, the Sony WH-1000XM6 — our top pick for premium sound — are over $100 off.

Recent findings suggest that as someone who tests headphones year-round and is heading into her sixth year covering Black Friday at Mashable, I only write about deals that are actual deals. That means double-checking accurate list prices, using my price history knowledge from looking at headphone product listings every time I open my work laptop, and consulting the Mashable shopping team's collective knowledge of historical pricing. This year, my criteria also include an awareness of price increases that have affected nearly every area of tech.

Recent findings suggest that with all that in mind, those two aforementioned deals — and the ones below — are the best headphones deals you'll find on Black Friday. If and when any more notable deals drop, you'll be sure to find them on this list.

It's basically impossible to beat the value of this Bose deal, which brings the first-generation Ultras down to a record-low price of $229. Not only is that a $200 markdown — it's $120 cheaper than the next-gen Ultras, which have minimal differences from the first-gen option. In other words, if you're looking for flagship performance at mid-range prices, this is the deal to get. Recent findings suggest that you don’t have to spend Bose money for a pair of everyday headphones. At $38, the Sony WH-CH530 offer up to 55 hours of battery life, multipoint Bluetooth for connecting to two devices at once, and a quick-charge feature that gets you another 90 minutes of listening after just three minutes plugged in. These are on-ear headphones, and they don’t have active noise cancellation, so they’re better suited to shoppers who want an inexpensive pair for music and taking calls.

These headphones also hit the market just this past September, and at $38, are already matching the record-low of their predecessor and a former budget favorite of ours, the Sony CH-520N.

The Sony WH-1000XM6 are our top pick for premium sound, and the discount makes their flagship price a little easier to stomach. Mashable’s testing found improved sound quality, particularly on vocal-heavy tracks, along with excellent active noise cancellation and a comfortable fit for longer listening sessions. Sony also brought back the folding design, so these are easier to pack than the XM5s. Battery life hasn’t improved from the previous generation, but you still get up to 30 hours with ANC on. At $348, these headphones are down to a record-low price, beating their former sale price of $378 that we already recommended picking up. In other words, you're not likely to grab a much better deal than this if you've been waiting on buying Sony's flagship headphones.

If you don't care about having the latest and greatest headphones, you can also get the previous generation XM5s on sale for Black Friday for an astonishingly low $169.99.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The EU registered 279,799 battery-electric cars in October, up 61.4%, while petrol and diesel sales each fell about 30%, leaving EVs almost 70,000 ahead of the two combined, ACEA data reveals.
  • Electric cars outsold petrol and diesel cars combined in the EU in October, InsideEVs reported, based on figures from the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA).
  • Recent findings suggest that the EU registered 279,799 battery-electric cars last month, up 61.4% from a year earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The EU registered 279,799 battery-electric cars in October, up 61.4%, while petrol and diesel sales each fell about 30%, leaving EVs almost 70,000 ahead of the two combined, ACEA data reveals. Hybrids still lead the market, and combustion cars remain ahead for the year so far.

Electric cars outsold petrol and diesel cars combined in the EU in October, InsideEVs reported, based on figures from the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA).

Recent findings suggest that the EU registered 279,799 battery-electric cars last month, up 61.4% from a year earlier. Petrol sales fell 30% to 158,970 and diesel sales fell 31% to 51,177. That left EVs almost 70,000 cars ahead of the two combined.

A year earlier, petrol and diesel cars outsold EVs by about 127,000, InsideEVs calculated. Electric cars took 29.8% of the EU market in October, while total registrations rose 2.6% to 939,447. A growing range of cheaper models is giving buyers more reasons to switch.

Germany and France drove much of the jump. Germany registered 94,086 EVs, up 60.7%, and France 61,958, up 79.4%. In June, EVs outsold every other fuel in Germany for the first time.

Recent findings suggest that chinese and US brands gained too. BYD registered 30,974 cars in the EU in October, up 128%, as Chinese carmakers push into Europe. Tesla’s registrations rose 83.5% to 10,166.

It has been revealed that hybrids are still the EU’s best-sellers. Full and mild hybrids took 36% of registrations from January to October, against 23.4% for battery-electric cars. Their popularity helps explain why Brussels has proposed softening its 2035 target so some can stay on sale.

According to recent reports, petrol and diesel cars also still lead for the year so far, with 2.61 million registrations to 2.21 million for EVs. A year ago, they outsold EVs by more than two to one. In August, electric cars took 29% of new registrations across Europe.

#4377. Tech Report: 4 Security Devices I Rely On for Front Porch and Delivery Protection

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (778 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 4 Security Devices I Rely On for Front Porch and Delivery Protection

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (778 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason.
  • From protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without.
  • Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason. That’s where burglars first try, too, and research demonstrates thieves can be deterred with the presence of a security cam — but security technology can do so much more.

From protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without. Take a look to see what your porch could use, too, and the tech options I recommend looking at.

Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock. Smart locks allow you to control your front door lock from anywhere using your phone, as well as creating temporary passes for guests. They can support digital wallet keys for touchless unlocking, and many have keypads or fingerprint readers. Plus, you can enable settings like auto-locking, so you never have to worry about forgetting to lock the door.

Smart locks come in two flavors: retrofits that leave your deadbolt largely intact and only replace your indoor thumb turn, and full deadbolt replacements that give you latest locking power, inside and out. Don’t worry about installation: If you’ve never installed a deadbolt before, the process is generally easy and doesn’t take much time. I have a full guide where you can find more details.

Say goodbye to dusty doorbells of the past. Today’s high-tech doorbells do far more than chime: Video doorbells keep an eye on your front porch, while also giving you a two-way audio intercom right on your phone to hold a conversation — or even let an LLM do the talking for you.

Video doorbells also have particularly useful object recognition features, sometimes even for free. That includes recognizing packages and alerting you whenever one shows up at your door, or when one suddenly vanishes. Video storage options can save recordings of key events, so you can check who came to the door if you need to.

Sources indicate that these advanced doorbells come in both wired and wireless versions. I’m a fan of the battery-powered, wireless models, which you can set and angle to get just the right look at your porch, doormat and other key places. Many can also work with your current door chime, although you probably don’t need it anymore with phone-based chimes.

Yale’s delivery boxes are larger, so you need room for them in the right spots.

Package theft concerns have reignited a centuries-old tradition of protecting mail. Today’s modern delivery boxes are specifically designed to allow delivery people to put packages inside, but make it difficult or impossible for thieves to take packages out, through clever lock models, auto-locking, smart controls and other various tricks.

I’ve been using a delivery box myself for a couple of years and find it very handy, as long as you have the space by your door. Some versions even come weighted or screwed down if you’re worried about a porch pirate absconding with the entire box. It’s a good idea to put notes in your deliveries to use the box, since despite signs not all delivery people will notice it’s there.

As a final plus, these boxes also keep your packages protected from the elements, which is nice when you live in an area that gets frequent winter snowstorms, as I do.

Smart bulbs are cheap, support multiple voice assistants and have lots of fun tricks.

Where front doors exist, there’s usually a light nearby, like an overhead porch light or a wall-mounted lamp, to illuminate the entryway and surrounding area. These lights can also get a major makeover if you switch to an LED smart bulb, which are available as both BR30 floodlights and standard A19 home bulbs.

Sources indicate that these lights also give you phone app controls, which is more important than it might seem. With my apps, I can control brightness, set schedules for bulbs to turn on or off, and even adjust the color to whatever I want, say for a holiday event. All it takes is screwing in the bulb and connecting it to Wi-Fi, so you can be done in seconds.

If you feel like experimenting, you can usually link smart bulbs to other devices, too. For example, you could set the light to turn on automatically when a smart lock is unlocked, or when a security system is disarmed.

Now that your front porch is up to date, take a look at the latest home AI tricks I’ve found are actually worth using and how to get them.

HomeKit Weekly: Meross’s newly introduced presence sensor splits a room into three zones for Apple Home

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Presence sensors tell Apple Home when someone is in a particular room, which is awesome for running automations based on that.
  • HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.
  • According to recent reports, you’ll set the zones in the Meross iPhone app during setup, choosing a distance for each.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Presence sensors tell Apple Home when someone is in a particular room, which is awesome for running automations based on that. They don’t tell it where in the room you are, though. That’s why these types of automations end up being all-or-nothing type things: you walk into a room, and every light comes on at full brightness, whether you came in to read at your desk or to grab something off the counter. The Meross MS605 splits its detection range into three distance zones, and each of them indicates up in Apple Home as its own presence sensor so you can build automations around them.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

According to recent reports, you’ll set the zones in the Meross iPhone app during setup, choosing a distance for each. Once the Meross MS605 is in Apple Home (via Matter), all three appear as separate presence sensors, and you can build automations for each individually. If you only want two, disable the third in the Meross app, and it disappears from the Home app as well.

Sources indicate that A bathroom is the obvious use case here for early mornings. Set the far zone to turn a lamp on at 5% and the near zone to bring up an overhead light, etc.

Industry observers note that the same idea works anywhere the room has more than one job. A hallway can light the path dim from the far zone, then go to 100% when you get close. An office can keep the overheads on while you’re anywhere in the room and turn on the desk lamp when you actually sit down as well. I find it incredibly useful for overall dimming, though.

The Meross MS605 uses mmWave radar and PIR together, which is the current best practice for presence detection. Meross claims the radar picks up micro-movement, so it knows you’re there when you’re sitting still, and the PIR filters out things that move but aren’t warm, like curtains and a robot vacuum. There’s also a radar-only setting if you want it as well.

It has been revealed that range is up to about 20 feet for motion and 13 feet for presence, with each zone configurable within those limits. There’s a built-in light sensor, too, so you can gate your lighting automations based on actual room brightness instead of guessing when you’ll want it with a sunset/sunrise trigger.

The Meross MS605 is IP67-rated and operates from -4 to 140 degrees Fahrenheit, so a covered porch, a garage, or a basement is all fair game for placing the sensor.

The initial setup runs via the Meross app over Bluetooth, and the app is required afterward. Zones, sensitivity, presence-and-absence timing, recalibration, and firmware updates all live in it. Day-to-day control and automation happen in Apple Home, but anything you want to tune requires going back.

One minor thing to know before you mount somewhere hard to reach: changing settings over Bluetooth requires pressing a physical button on top of the sensor, so keep that in mind when configuring your settings and initially placing it.

Recent findings suggest that the Meross MS605 unlocks some unique use cases with its three zones. Three zones from one sensor is a new automation tool, and the IP67 rating means you can put it in places other presence sensors can’t go. It’s powered by a CR123A battery, which is included in the box.

The Meross MS605 is available on Amazon.
